text: They led me. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a vast building of gray stone. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose doorway was richly carved. <break time="0.8s" /> But badly broken and worn by time. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside was a great hall. <break time="0.8s" /> Full of tables made of polished stone. <break time="0.8s" /> On which lay heaps of fruit. <break time="0.8s" /> That I had never seen before. <break time="0.8s" /> The little people sat down on cushions. <break time="0.8s" /> And ate with their hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Throwing the peel and stalks. <break time="0.8s" /> Into round openings in the tables. <break time="0.8s" /> Following their example. <break time="0.8s" /> I ate too. <break time="0.8s" /> For I was very hungry and thirsty. <break time="0.8s" /> After my long journey through time. <break time="0.8s" /> Later I learned. <break time="0.8s" /> That these people ate nothing but fruit. <break time="0.8s" /> As the horses, cattle, and dogs of our age. <break time="0.8s" /> Had all disappeared. <break time="0.8s" /> I tried to learn their language. <break time="0.8s" /> By holding up a piece of fruit. <break time="0.8s" /> And asking its name. <break time="0.8s" /> Which made them laugh with delight. <break time="0.8s" /> But they were like small children. <break time="0.8s" /> Who soon grow tired of a game. <break time="0.8s" /> And after a few minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> They would wander away from me. <break time="0.8s" /> Seldom had I seen. <break time="0.8s" /> Such gentle people. <break time="0.8s" /> But I soon noticed. <break time="0.8s" /> Something strange about them. <break time="0.8s" /> A complete lack of interest. <break time="0.8s" /> In anything new.
